blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves multimodal reasoning, but group-relative policy optimization broadcasts a single sequence-level advantage to every token of a response, although errors usually localize to a few decisive steps. Recent self-distilled variants refine credit with a teacher--student likelihood gap. However, this signal cannot tell whether it relies on the image or on a language shortcut, and is applied uniformly even when the teacher is uninformative. To address this, we propose Pairwise token contrast and Adaptive trajectory ConfidencE (PACE). Pairwise token contrast scores each response under four teacher views, crossing a correct or incorrect answer hint with the image present or removed, and compares the two hints for every token, which cancels shifts shared by both hints and reveals whether the token's support relies on the image. Adaptive trajectory confidence measures how well the teacher predicts each response given the correct hint and the image, normalizes this score within the batch, and uses it to set how far the token contrast redistributes credit within that response. PACE achieves the best average accuracy on three backbones and ranks first on all evaluated multimodal reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Experiments show that both components matter: replacing pairwise token contrast with a single-view signal underperforms our method, while adaptive trajectory confidence adds further improvement.
blocks.zh: 具有可核查奖励的强化学习(RLVR)改进了多模式推理,但集团关系政策优化向每个响应符号播送单一序列级的优势,尽管错误通常被本地化为几个决定性步骤. 最近自我消化的变体以师生概率差距完善了信用。 然而,这个信号无法分辨它是依赖于图像还是语言快捷键,即使在老师不知情的情况下也统一应用. 为了解决这个问题,我们提议对等符号对比和适应性轨迹自信(PACE)。 平面符号对比在四个老师视图下对每个响应进行分数,用所显示的或被删除的图像交叉一个正确或错误的答案提示,并比较每个符号的两个提示,这可以取消两个提示共享的切换,并揭示该符号的支持是否依赖于图像. 适应性轨迹信任度测量 老师如何根据正确的提示和图像 预测每个反应, 使这个分数在批量中正常化, 计算机设备行动伙伴关系在三个主干线上实现了最佳平均准确性,在所有经过评价的多模式推理基准中排名第一,采用Qune3-VL-8B-Instruct。 实验表明,这两个组成部分都很重要:用单视信号取代对偶信号,使我们的方法表现不佳,而适应性轨迹信心则会进一步提高。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: RLVR has emerged as a powerful approach for improving reasoning in large language models ( Guo et al., 2025 ) . A rule-based verifier scores sampled responses, and group-relative policy optimization methods such as GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) convert these verifier rewards into learning signals without requiring a learned reward model. This paradigm extends naturally to vision-language models, improving visual mathematics and multimodal reasoning ( Huang et al., 2026b ; Meng et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: RLVR已成为改进大语言模型推理的有力方法(Guo等,2025年). 基于规则的核查者得分抽样回答,GRPO(Shao等,2024年)等群体相对政策优化方法将这些核查者奖励转换为学习信号而不需要学习奖励模式. 这一范式自然延伸至视觉语言模型,改进了视觉数学和多模式推理(黄等,2026b;孟等,2025.).

blocks.en: Self-distilled RLVR refines the sequence-level advantage of GRPO at the token level, as in RLSD ( Yang et al., 2026 ) and RLCSD ( Pan et al., 2026 ) . A periodically synchronized copy of the policy scores each sampled response under a privileged context, typically the ground-truth answer, and the resulting teacher–student likelihood gap reweights individual tokens. This lets credit concentrate on the few steps where long multimodal reasoning chains usually go wrong, such as a misread chart label or a single arithmetic mistake.
blocks.zh: 自消自灭的RLVR完善了GRPO在象征层面的序列级优势,如RLSD(Yang等,2026年)和RLCSD(Pan等,2026年). 一份定期同步的政策拷贝在特权背景下对每个抽样反应进行评分,通常是地面真实的答案,由此产生的师生概率差距会重新对单个符号进行加权。 这使得信用集中在长多模式推理链通常会出错的几个步骤上,例如误读图表标签或单一算术错误.

blocks.en:
Although these approaches provide dense token-level supervision, they face two unaddressed challenges in multimodal reasoning. On the one hand, they derive this supervision from a contrast along a single modality.
RLCSD varies only the textual answer hint, while visually grounded signals ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Huang et al., 2026a ) vary only the image.
On the other hand, they apply the same fixed weighting strategy to every rollout trajectory, while the teacher is confident on some trajectories and uninformative on others.
Together, these two challenges aggravate the drift of the teacher–student gap. The signal comes from a single view and is applied with equal strength to every response. Any shift in the teacher’s or the student’s likelihood during training passes directly into the token weights.
blocks.zh:
虽然这些办法提供了密集的象征性监督,但它们在多式联运推理方面面临两个未解决的挑战。 一方面,它们从一种单一模式的对比中得出这种监督。
RLCSD只改变文字答案提示,而视网膜信号(Wang等,2026b; Huang et al., 2026a))只改变图像.
另一方面,他们在每个推出轨迹时都采用同样的固定加权策略,而老师则对一些轨迹有信心,对另一些轨迹则不知情.
这两种挑战共同加重了师生差距。 信号来自单一的视角,并且以同等强度被应用到每个响应中. 教师或学生在培训期间可能发生的任何变化都直接进入象征性加权。

blocks.en: To address these limitations, we propose PACE, a method for enhancing multimodal RLVR with two components: pairwise token contrast and adaptive trajectory confidence, as shown in Figure 1 . Pairwise token contrast scores each sampled response under four teacher views that cross correct vs. incorrect answer hints with full vs. null vision. Comparing the two hints under full vision and under null vision gives two correctness contrasts per token, which we combine into a single token contrast. The null-vision contrast exposes whether the correctness signal persists without the image, and because the two views in each contrast differ only in the hint, offsets shared by both hints, including drift in the teacher’s overall confidence, cancel out. Adaptive trajectory confidence measures how much better the teacher predicts each response under the full-information view than under the degraded views, normalizes this confidence within the batch, and uses it to set how far the token contrast redistributes credit among the tokens of each response. Our contributions are as follows: • We propose pairwise token contrast, which removes the dependence on the student’s likelihood, cancels confidence drift shared by both hints, and assigns credit without biasing it toward either the image or the text. • We propose adaptive trajectory confidence, which treats distinct trajectories differently by applying the token contrast more strongly where the teacher is confident and less where it is uninformative, remains stable as the teacher’s confidence drifts during training, and preserves the sign and mean of every response’s advantage. • Extensive experiments show that PACE obtains the best average accuracy on all three main backbones across five multimodal reasoning benchmarks. We provide ablations showing that pairwise token contrast and adaptive trajectory confidence both contribute to the gains.
blocks.zh: 为了克服这些局限性,我们提议采用PACE这一方法,加强多式RLVR,其中包含两个组成部分:成对符号对比和适应性轨迹信心,如图1所示。 对等符号对比在四个老师视图下对每个被抽取的回答进行分数,这些老师视图用完全对等的视觉交叉对错的回答提示. 在全视和虚视下比较两个提示,每个符号都给出两个正确性对比,我们结合到一个符号对比中. 虚视对比暴露出正确性信号是否在没有图像的情况下持续,而且由于每种对比中的两种观点仅在提示上有所不同,抵消了两种提示的共通性,包括教师总体信心的漂移,从而取消. 适应性轨迹信任度衡量老师在全信息视角下对每个响应的预测比在已退化的视角下要好得多,使批次中的这种信心正常化,并用它来设定符号对比在每一个响应的符号中重新分配信用的程度. - 我们的捐助如下: 我们提出双向符号对比,消除了对学生可能性的依赖,取消了两个提示共享的自信漂移,并在不偏袒图像或文字的情况下分配信用。 我们提出适应性轨迹自信,通过在教师自信的地方更强烈地运用象征对比来不同地对待不同的轨迹,在培训期间教师信心漂移时保持稳定,并保持每种反应优势的标志和取向。 二. 支助 广泛的实验表明,计算机设备行动伙伴关系在五个多式联运推理基准的所有三个主要主干线上获得最佳平均准确性。 我们提供的浮雕表明,对等的比喻和适应性轨迹的信心都有助于取得这些成果。

blocks.en: 2 Related Works
blocks.zh: 2 相关工程

blocks.en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable outcome avoids a learned reward model when correctness can be checked with rules. GRPO estimates relative advantages from multiple responses to the same prompt without a separate critic ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , and multimodal variants apply this recipe to visual mathematics and general visual reasoning ( Huang et al., 2026b ; Meng et al., 2025 ) . These methods generally broadcast a sequence-level advantage across response tokens. PACE keeps the verifier and group advantage unchanged and assigns that credit at token level.
blocks.zh: 在用规则检查正确性时,用可核查的结果加强学习可避免学习奖励模式。 GRPO估计在没有单独评论者的情况下对同一快件作出多回响应的相对好处(Shao等,2024年),多式变体将这种配方应用于视觉数学和一般视觉推理(Huang等,2026b;Meng等,2025年). 这些方法一般通过响应符广播序列级优势. 计算机设备行动伙伴关系保持核查人和集团优势不变,并将这一信用额划入象征性水平。

blocks.en: On-policy distillation ( Agarwal et al., 2024 ) and its self-distilled variants evaluate responses sampled by the student itself ( Zhao et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Hübotter et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ; Pan et al., 2026 ) . Recent work makes the same broad move toward finer credit: VCSD uses image-content removal to form a visual contrast and distills a sharpened token distribution ( Liang et al., 2026 ) ; GCPO contrasts positive and negative prompts and derives token advantages from predictive divergence ( Li et al., 2026b ) ; PEPO combines a hidden-state perception prior with token entropy ( Li et al., 2026c ) ; and CEPO, the closest contemporaneous method, contrasts a correct-answer teacher with a wrong-answer teacher built from an already-rejected rollout to flag decisive tokens on multimodal math reasoning ( Heakl et al., 2026 ) . These methods differ from PACE in both signal and objective. VCSD does not condition the contrast on correctness, GCPO does not factor out generic visual sensitivity with a full/null factorial design, PEPO uses perception–exploration statistics rather than answer-conditioned teacher contrasts, and CEPO’s answer contrast holds the image fixed rather than crossing it with a full/null vision axis. PACE uses answer-conditioned, vision-dependent token contrast for sign-preserving GRPO credit assignment, not as a standalone distillation target.
blocks.zh: 政策上蒸馏(Agarwal等,2024年)及其自蒸分解的变体评价了学生自己所采样的答复(赵等,2026年;杨等,2026年;Hübotter等,2026年;李等,2026a;潘等,2026年). 最近的工作也向更精细的功劳做出了同样的广泛举动:VCSD使用图像-内容去除来形成视觉对比并提炼出更清晰的符号分布(Liang等,2026年;GCPO对比正反的提示并从预测差异(Li等,2026年b)中获得符号优势;PEPO将一种隐藏状态的感想与象征式的肽(Li等,2026年c)结合;CEPO是当时最接近的方法,它将一个正确回答的老师与一个已经被排斥的推开以标出在多模式数学推理上的决定性符号(Heakl等,2026年c)对比。 这些方法在信号和客观上都与PACE不同. VCSD不以正确性作为对比条件,GCPO不以全/虚因子设计来考虑通用视觉敏感性,PEPO使用感知-探索统计而不是回答条件的教师对比,CEPO的答案对比持有固定的图像而不是用全/虚视轴来跨越. 计算机设备行动伙伴关系对保留标志的GPRO信用任务使用有解答条件的、依赖视觉的符号对比,而不是作为独立的蒸馏目标。

blocks.en: PAPO, VPPO, and propagation-aware visual retention prioritize visual dependence or retention during long-chain reasoning ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Huang et al., 2026a ; Gong et al., 2026 ) ; reflection-centric systems instead add explicit rethink or re-attention stages ( Wang et al., 2026a ; Wan et al., 2026 ; Yao et al., 2026 ; Jian et al., 2025 ; Chu et al., 2025 ) . Dependence alone is unsigned with respect to correctness, and reflection changes the sampled reasoning process. In contrast, PACE evaluates the already sampled response under correct/incorrect hints and full/null vision, then uses the resulting token contrast for token-level credit assignment without changing inference.
blocks.zh: PAPO、VPPO和可传播-感知视觉保留在长链推理中优先考虑视觉依赖或保留(Wang等,2026b; Huang等人,2026a;Gong等人,2026;以反射为中心的系统反而增加了明确的再思考或重新思考阶段(Wang等人,2026a; Wan等,2026;Yao等,2026;Jian等,2025;Chu等,2025; 依赖性本身在正确性方面没有签名,反射会改变抽样推理过程. 相形之下,PACE在正确/不正确提示和完整/虚幻视野下评价已经被抽取的响应,然后在不改变推论的情况下,将由此而来的信使对比用于信使级信用分配.

blocks.en: 5.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 5.1 实验设置

blocks.en: We compare PACE with main multimodal RLVR methods. GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) is the baseline that broadcasts a uniform sequence-level advantage to every token. OPSD ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) trains the student policy by the privileged teacher with self-generated rollouts. RLSD ( Yang et al., 2026 ) and RLCSD ( Pan et al., 2026 ) are self-distilled RLVR methods that derive token-level credit from answer-conditioned teacher–student contrasts, and are the closest to our approach. PAPO ( Wang et al., 2026b ) and VPPO ( Huang et al., 2026a ) inject visually grounded signals into the RL objective, addressing grounding from a direction orthogonal to token credit.
blocks.zh: 我们比较PACE与主要的多式RLVR方法. GRPO(Shao等,2024年)是向每个信使广播统一序列级优势的基线. OPSD (Zhao等, 2026) 由特权教师通过自发推出来培训学生政策. RLSD(Yang等人,2026年)和RLCSD(Pan等人,2026年)是自消自消的RLVR方法,它们从有解答条件的教师那里获得象征性的信用 — — 学生对比,并且是最接近我们的方法的. PAPO(Wang等人,2026年b)和VPPO(Huang等人,2026年a)向RL目标注入视基信号,解决从正向到象征信用的地基问题。

blocks.en: PACE, GRPO, RLSD, RLCSD, PAPO, and VPPO are trained under a shared configuration on the MMFineReason-123K training split by RLSD, which derives from MMFineReason ( Lin et al., 2026 ) and keeps only the final conclusion after the </think> tag as supervision. All methods are trained for 200 optimization steps with 8 rollouts per prompt (Appendix 3 ). To evaluate scalability and generalizability across diverse architectures and model scales, we use Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ( Bai et al., 2025a ) , Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct ( Bai et al., 2025b ) , and InternVL3.5-4B ( Wang et al., 2025 ) for training. OPSD uses its original implementation with rank-64 LoRA ( Hu et al., 2021 ) and the ms-swift trainer (Appendix 4 ). Checkpoint selection is based on the training reward over the final 50 steps.
blocks.zh: PACE,GRPO,RLSD,RLCSD,PAPO,和VPPO在MMFineReason-123K训练中按照由RLSD分割的共享配置进行训练,该组合取自MMFineReason(Lin等,2026年)并仅保留了"/想"标记后的最后结论作为监督. 所有方法都经过了200个优化步骤的培训,每个快取8个推出(附录3 . 为了评估各种建筑和模型尺度的可扩展性和可通用性,我们使用Qune3-VL-8B-Instruct(Bai等,2025a) , Quen2.5-VL-7B-指示 (Bai等, 2025b), 和 InternVL3.5-4B (Wang等, 2025) 用于培训. OPSD使用它最初的执行有军衔-64 LoRA(Hu等,2021年)和MS-swift教练器(附录4 . 选择检查站的依据是最后50个步骤的培训奖励。

blocks.en: We evaluate on five multimodal reasoning benchmarks. GSM8K-V ( Yuan et al., 2025 ) renders grade-school math word problems as images, directly testing whether a model reads quantitative content from pixels. LogicVista ( Xiao et al., 2024 ) tests logical reasoning over visual scenes. MMMU ( Yue et al., 2024 ) is a college-level, multi-discipline multimodal understanding benchmark. MathVision ( Wang et al., 2024 ) collects competition-level mathematical problems in visual contexts. MathVista ( Lu et al., 2024 ) aggregates a broad range of mathematical and visual reasoning tasks. All benchmarks are evaluated with VLMEvalKit ( Duan et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 我们评估了五个多式联运推理基准。 GSM8K-V(Yuan等,2025年)将年级数学词问题作为图像,直接测试一个模型是否从像素读取了定量内容. LogicVista (Xiao等, 2024) 测试逻辑推理比视觉场景. MMMU(Yue等,2024年)是大学一级,多学科的多模式理解基准. Math Vision (Wang等, 2024)在视觉背景下收集竞争层次的数学问题. 数学维斯塔 (Lu等,2024)综合了广泛的数学和视觉推理任务. 所有基准都用VLMEvalKit(Duan等人,2024年)加以评估。

blocks.en: 5.2 Main Results
blocks.zh: 5.2 主要成果

blocks.en: PACE is best on every benchmark with 8B model. As shown in Table 1 , on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, PACE ranks first on all five benchmarks and reaches 58.47% on average, +6.38 over Base, +3.64 over GRPO, and +1.22 over the strongest baseline VPPO. The gains over Base are largest on LogicVista (+8.95), MathVision (+8.22), and MMMU (+7.67), and smallest on MathVista (+1.90), where all methods lie within 2.7 points of each other. VPPO is second on every benchmark, so the margin over it (0.60–1.79 points per benchmark) is the tightest comparison. PACE reaches it at about a third of VPPO’s per-step training time, as detailed in Appendix B.9 . Appendix D visualizes PACE’s token credit on three examples.
blocks.zh: 计算机设备行动伙伴关系在每个基准上最好采用8B模型。 如表1所示,在Qune3-VL-8B-指令中,计算机设备行动伙伴关系在所有五个基准中名列前茅,平均达到58.47%,在基数上为+6.38,在GRPO上为+3.64,在最强基线上为+1.22。 在LogicVista(+8.95)、Math Vision(+8.22)和MMMU(+7.67)上的收益最大,在MathVista(+1.90)上的收益最小,所有方法都位于相距2.7分以内。 VPPO在每个基准上位居第二,因此比值(每个基准0.60–1.79分)是最严格的比较. 如附录B.9所详述的,计算机设备行动伙伴关系在每步培训时间的三分之一左右达到。 附 录 D可视化PACE在三个例子上的象征性功劳.

blocks.en:
Pairwise token contrast improves over teacher–student gaps. RLSD and RLCSD share PACE’s training stack and differ mainly in how token credit is computed, so this comparison isolates the credit signal. PACE outperforms RLSD by 3.09 points and RLCSD by 3.96 points on average, with the largest gaps on LogicVista (+5.59 over RLSD, +6.26 over RLCSD) and MathVision (+4.11 and +5.06). RLCSD, which contrasts correct and incorrect hints without the vision axis or adaptive trajectory confidence, gains 2.42 points over Base, fewer than GRPO (2.74), while PACE gains 6.38. OPSD, trained with LoRA adapters in a separate framework, falls below Base, which we attribute to its different optimization setup rather than to on-policy distillation itself. The same pattern holds on the other two backbones: RLSD improves over GRPO by at most 0.55 points
, while PACE improves over GRPO by 3.64, 1.48, and 1.12 points.

校对:Soup RLSD和RLCSD共享PACE的训练堆并主要在象征性信用计算方式上有所不同,因此这一比较隔离了信用信号. PACE平均比RLSD高出3.09分,而RLCSD高出3.96分,在LogicVista(比RLSD高出5.59分,比RLCSD高出6.26分)和Math Vision(比4.11分和+5.06分)上差距最大. RLCSD,与没有视觉轴或适应性轨迹信心的正确和不正确的提示形成对比,比基数(GRPO)(2.74)得2.42分,而PACE则得6.38分. OPSD与LORA适配器在一个单独的框架中经过了培训,它落在了Base下面,我们将此归因于它不同的优化设置,而不是政策上提炼本身. 其他两个主干部分也有同样的模式:RLSD比GRPO改进了最多0.55分
,而PACE则比GRPO提高3.64分,1.48分和1.12分.

blocks.en: PACE leads across different backbones. The advantage is not specific to Qwen3-VL-8B. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, PACE achieves the best average accuracy (45.17%, +4.04 over Base), ahead of VPPO (44.17%), RLSD (43.90%), and GRPO (43.69%). It ranks first on MMMU, MathVision, and MathVista and is within 0.11 points of the best method on GSM8K-V and LogicVista. On InternVL3.5-4B, which comes from a different model family, PACE again achieves the best average accuracy (48.00%, +2.05 over Base) and ranks first on four of five benchmarks, with RLSD only marginally better on GSM8K-V (15.92 vs. 15.54). On both backbones, PACE improves over Base on every benchmark rather than on a single task.
blocks.zh: PACE领导不同骨干. 其优点并非是Quen3-VL-8B所特有的. 在Qun2.5-VL-7B-指令上,PACE实现了最佳平均精度(45.17%,比基数高+4.04),领先于VPPO(44.17%),RLSD(43.90%)和GRPO(43.69%). 它在MMMU,MathVision和MathVista上排名第一,在GSM8K-V和LogicVista上处于最佳方法的0.11分以内. 在来自不同型号家族的InternVL3.5-4B上,PACE再次实现了最佳平均精度(48.00%,比基数高+2.05),并在五个基准中的四个基准中排名第一,在GSM8K-V(15.92 vs 15.54)上RLSD只略好. 在两个支柱方面,计算机设备行动伙伴关系在每个基准上,而不是在一个单一任务上,都比基地有所改善。

blocks.en:
The gain over baselines narrows with smaller self-teachers. The gain of PACE over base model shrinks with backbone size: +6.38 points on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, +4.04 points on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, and +2.05 points on InternVL3.5-4B, while still remaining ahead of the strongest baseline.
Since the self-teacher is a copy of the policy, a smaller backbone is less able to solve the hard training problems even with privileged hints, which makes its token contrasts noisier and limits how much token-level credit assignment can add over uniform credit.
blocks.zh:
超过基线的增益与较小的自学教师相缩小. PACE优于基础模型的增益收缩了骨干大小:Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct上的+6.38分;Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct上的+4.04分;InternVL3.5-4B上的+2.05分,同时仍然处于最强基线前.
由于自学老师是政策的复制品,一个更小的骨干即使有特权的暗示也不太能够解决硬培训问题,这使得其象征性地对比了名人,并限制了象征性的信用分配能比统一信用多出多少.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
This paper presents PACE, a method for self-distilled multimodal reasoning RLVR that assigns credit at two levels: pairwise token contrast decides which tokens of a response receive more credit, and adaptive trajectory confidence decides how far that credit is redistributed on each response.
Our experiments show that hint contrasts give more stable token credit than single-view signals, which drift during training. Normalizing trajectory confidence within each batch keeps the mixing rate stable throughout training.
With these designs, PACE achieves the best average accuracy on evaluated benchmarks with models across different model families and model sizes from 4B to 8B.

blocks.en: Pairwise token contrast cancels only offsets shared by paired hints, and the null-vision intervention cannot rule out language shortcuts that correlate with the correct answer. The trajectory confidence that sets the mixing rate measures how well the teacher separates the full-information view from the degraded ones, not whether a response actually needs the image, so a high mixing rate does not guarantee visual grounding (Appendix B.5 ). The sign- and mean-preserving properties hold for the token weights, not for the clipped PPO update. Gains are smaller on smaller backbones such as InternVL3.5-4B. On Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, PACE does not achieve the best average (Appendix C.2 ). We attribute this to the training data. Following RLSD, MMFineReason-123K keeps only problems that Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking fails in all four rollouts, and on such hard problems smaller self-teachers remain unreliable even with privileged hints, so their token contrasts are noisier. Our experiments cover multimodal mathematical and logical reasoning with verifiable answers. Whether the gains transfer to other tasks remains to be tested. Finally, scoring four teacher views adds training cost, although inference is unaffected.

blocks.en: RLVR uses automatically checkable outcomes to avoid dense process supervision. GRPO estimates a relative advantage from multiple responses to one prompt without a separate value model ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , while subsequent systems study exploration, clipping, and training stability ( Guo et al., 2025 ) . Multimodal RLVR transfers this recipe to visual mathematics and general visual reasoning ( Huang et al., 2026b ; Meng et al., 2025 ) . The common limitation relevant to PACE is that a scalar response-level advantage is broadcast to every valid response token. PACE keeps this verifier-defined direction and changes only the allocation of credit within the sampled trajectory.
blocks.zh: RLVR使用自动可核查的结果来避免密集的流程监督. GRPO估计从多个响应到一个没有单独价值模型的快报的相对优势(Shao等,2024年),而后来的系统研究探索,剪接和培训稳定性(Guo等,2025年). 多式联运 RLVR将这种配方转移至视觉数学和一般视觉推理(Huang等,2026b;Meng等,2025.). 与PACE相关的共同限制是,每个有效响应符号都广播出斯卡尔克响应级别优势. 计算机设备行动伙伴关系保持这一经核查者界定的方向,仅改变抽样轨迹内的信用分配。

blocks.en: On-policy distillation trains on prefixes and responses sampled by the student, reducing the mismatch between training trajectories and inference behavior ( Agarwal et al., 2024 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) . Self-distilled RLVR methods instead let a single model play both roles: an EMA or periodically synchronized copy of the actor is given privileged context and used to score the same realized tokens. RLSD uses a privileged answer-conditioned teacher–student likelihood gap as a bounded token-credit signal while anchoring the update sign to the verifier ( Yang et al., 2026 ) ; SDPO instead conditions the self-teacher on rich textual feedback (e.g., an error explanation) rather than the ground-truth answer and distills the feedback-informed distribution densely into the student ( Hübotter et al., 2026 ) ; SRPO observes that self-distillation supervision is uninformative on already-correct rollouts and routes correct samples to GRPO while only incorrect samples receive dense self-distillation, with an entropy-aware weight on the teacher target ( Li et al., 2026a ) . RLCSD contrasts correct and incorrect answer hints to suppress components shared by both conditions ( Pan et al., 2026 ) . PACE extends this line by asking whether the correctness contrast is specifically supported by the visual input.
blocks.zh: 由学生所抽取的前缀和应答的政策分馏列车,减少了训练轨迹与推论行为之间的不匹配(Agarwal等,2024;赵等,2026). 自行消化的RLVR方法则让一个单一的模型发挥两种作用:一个EMA或定期同步复制的演员被赋予特权上下文并用来分出相同的已实现的符号. RLSD在将更新信号锁定到验证器(Yang等人,2026年)时,使用一种特权性的解答条件教师-学生概率差距作为限定符号-信用信号;SDPO则以丰富的文字反馈(例如错误解释)而不是地面真实的答案作为自我教师的条件,并将反馈知情的分布密集地分解到学生中(Hübotter等人,2026年);SRPO指出,自我消化监督在已经正确的推广上是没有成型的,并且将样本纠正到GRPO的路径,而只有不正确的样本获得密集的自消化,教师目标上具有内涵感分量(Li等人,2026a年) 。 。 。 。 RLCSD对比了正确和不正确的答案提示来压制两个条件共享的组件(Pan等,2026.). PACE通过询问正确性对比是否由视觉输入具体支持来延长此行.

blocks.en: Several contemporaneous papers also move beyond uniform sequence advantages. VCSD removes image content to create a visual contrast between original and content-erased inputs, then distills a sharpened full token distribution ( Liang et al., 2026 ) . GCPO contrasts predictions under positive and negative prompts and uses a predictive-divergence statistic to form per-token advantages ( Li et al., 2026b ) . PEPO derives a perception prior from hidden-state similarity and combines it with token entropy through a smooth gate ( Li et al., 2026c ) . CEPO is the closest contemporaneous method: it also asks whether a token is favored by a correct answer hint and disfavored by an incorrect one, built from an existing rejected rollout in the same batch, and uses the resulting agreement as a decisive-token signal on multimodal math reasoning ( Heakl et al., 2026 ) . Orthogonally, a polarity–entropy analysis argues that token entropy upper-bounds how much hindsight credit a token can absorb and reallocates GRPO advantages by crossing this capacity term with reward polarity ( He et al., 2026 ) . PACE differs from all of these in three ways. First, its raw statistic is a four-view difference-in-differences: two correctness contrasts, Δ i , t \Delta_{i,t} under observed vision and Δ ¯ i , t \bar{\Delta}_{i,t} under nulled vision (Eq. ( 5 )), are combined into the token contrast c i , t c_{i,t} (Eq. ( 6 )), rather than relying on a single visual contrast, prompt divergence, perception–entropy score, or an answer contrast alone. Unlike CEPO, whose two teacher views vary only the answer hint with the image held fixed, PACE’s 2 × 2 2\times 2 design crosses the answer hint with a full/null vision axis, so it can attribute the correctness contrast to the visual input specifically rather than to the hint alone. Second, the positive/negative views are answer candidates, so the statistic tests visual support for correctness rather than generic input sensitivity or token entropy. Third, c i , t c_{i,t} is used as a detached signal for sign-preserving, mean-conserving GRPO token-level credit assignment; it is not itself a distillation target and is interpreted as a contrastive signal, not a causal effect.
blocks.zh: 一些同时期的论文也超越了统一的序列优势. VCSD去除图像内容,以在原始输入和内容时代输入之间形成视觉对比,再提炼出一个更精致的全符号发行(梁等,2026). GCPO在正和负提示下对比预测,并使用预测-潜水统计来形成每趾的优势(Li等,2026b.)。 PEPO从隐藏状态的相似性获得先有的感知,并通过平滑的门将它和符號 en相融合(Li等,2026c.). CEPO是同時最相近的方法:它也询问一个符号是否受到正确答案提示的偏好而受到不正确的提示而不满,它是从同一批中现有的被否决的推出而来,并将由此而来的协议作为多模式数学推理的决定性的切入信号(Heakl等,2026年). Orthogon,一种极性 - entropy 分析认为,象征式的entropy 上行意味着,通过通过奖励式的极性跨越这一能力术语,一个象征式的后视功值能够吸收和再分配GRPO的优势(He等人,2026年)。 计算机设备行动伙伴关系在三个方面与所有这些不同。 首先,它的原始统计是四相差异:两个正确性对比,在观测到的视线下为i, t\Delta_{i, t}在虚构的视线下为i, t\bar\Delta}_{i, t}在虚构的视线下(Eq. (5)), 合并成符号对比ci, t\(C_{i, t), 而不是依靠单一的视觉对比, 即时分辨, 感知- 成正比分, 或单靠答案对比. 与CEPO不同的是,CEPO的两种老师观点只改变与所持图像固定的解答提示,PACE的2×2 2.\times 2设计用全/虚视轴来跨出解答提示,因此它可以将正确性对比具体归因于视觉输入,而不只是提示. 其次,正/负观点是回答候选,因此统计测试视觉支持正确性,而不是通用输入敏感度或符号 en. 第三,c i,t c_{i,t 被作为去除的信号,用于保留标志,平均保存GRPO标志级信用分配;它本身不是一个分馏目标,被解释为一个对比信号,而不是因果关系.

blocks.en: PAPO and VPPO prioritize tokens with stronger visual dependence, and propagation-aware objectives study whether visual information survives along long multimodal chains ( Wang et al., 2026b ; Huang et al., 2026a ; Gong et al., 2026 ) . These methods motivate measuring vision-aware token signals, but visual dependence is unsigned with respect to the answer: a wrong interpretation can also be highly image-sensitive. PACE subtracts the visual sensitivity associated with an incorrect answer hint from the sensitivity associated with a correct hint, targeting correctness-aligned visual evidence.
blocks.zh: PAPO和VPPO对视觉依赖性较强的标志物进行优先排序,传播意识目标研究视觉信息是否沿长多模式链生存(Wang等,2026b; 黄等,2026a;龚等,2026. 这些方法激发了对能见度-知觉符号信号的测量,但视觉依赖性在回答上是没有签名的:错误的解释也可能是高度图像敏感的. PACE从与正确提示相联的敏感度中减去了与错误的答案提示相联的视觉灵敏度,瞄准正确性相通的视觉证据.

blocks.en: Another family of multimodal RL methods adds reflection, search, or explicit re-attention to recover missing visual evidence ( Wang et al., 2026a ; Wan et al., 2026 ; Yao et al., 2026 ; Jian et al., 2025 ; Chu et al., 2025 ) . Those approaches modify the reasoning process or introduce additional stages. PACE is complementary: it scores the trajectory already sampled by the policy under controlled answer and visual contexts, and uses the resulting token contrast to assign credit without adding an inference-time reflection module.
blocks.zh: 另一多式RL方法家族增加了反射、搜索或明确重复,以取回缺失的视觉证据(Wang等,2026a; Wan等,2026;Yao等,2026;Jian等,2025;Chu等,2025; 这些办法修改了推理程序或引入了其他阶段。 计算机设备行动伙伴关系是互补的:它在受控的答案和视觉上下文下对政策已经取样的轨迹进行评分,并使用由此产生的符号对比来分配信用,而不增加推论时间反射模块。

Cancellation of shared offsets. Let ℓ = log ⁡ π ¯ ​ ( y i , t | x , h , y i , < t ) \ell=\log\bar{\pi}(y_{i,t}|x,h,y_{i,<t}) denote a teacher log-probability under some view, with h h the hint of that view. As the student moves, the teacher π ¯ \bar{\pi} , fixed between refreshes, scores increasingly off-distribution responses, which may shift its log-probabilities. Suppose, as an idealization, that this shift is a common offset for both hint views: ℓ ′ = ℓ + δ \ell^{\prime}=\ell+\delta . Each correctness contrast Δ i , t \Delta_{i,t} compares positive and negative hints under the same visual context: Δ i , t ′ = ( ℓ i , t + , V + δ ) − ( ℓ i , t − , V + δ ) = Δ i , t . \Delta^{\prime}_{i,t}=\big(\ell^{+,V}_{i,t}+\delta\big)-\big(\ell^{-,V}_{i,t}+\delta\big)=\Delta_{i,t}. The shift δ \delta cancels because both branches of the contrast are affected equally. The same cancellation holds for Δ ¯ i , t \bar{\Delta}_{i,t} under the nulled-vision branch. Therefore, the combined token contrast c i , t = α ​ Δ i , t + β ​ Δ ¯ i , t c_{i,t}=\alpha\Delta_{i,t}+\beta\bar{\Delta}_{i,t} preserves the relative correctness signal while removing any offset shared by the paired hint views. Scope. This is an algebraic property of the contrast, not a claim about training dynamics. It removes only offsets common to both branches of a contrast. The teacher’s uncertainty may shift non-uniformly: the positive and negative hint branches may respond differently to off-distribution responses, and nulled-vision views may shift differently from full-vision ones. Such view-specific shifts are not removed, and we do not claim that c i , t c_{i,t} is robust to policy drift in general. What the cancellation does and does not imply. The cancellation does not mean that 𝔼 t ​ [ c i , t ] = 0 \mathbb{E}_{t}[c_{i,t}]=0 for a single trajectory or that the token contrast is zero-mean in a statistical sense. Instead, it means: • The token contrast c i , t c_{i,t} contains no offset that is shared by the paired hint views, because every view appears inside a contrast and such terms cancel in the subtraction. • The statistic is a relative quantity rather than a zero-mean one: it measures relative correctness support (the difference between how strongly the token supports the correct vs. incorrect answer), not an absolute confidence level. • More formally: if we decompose each log-probability into a trajectory-level mean and token deviation, ℓ i , t + , V = μ + , V + δ i , t + , V \ell^{+,V}_{i,t}=\mu^{+,V}+\delta^{+,V}_{i,t} with trajectory mean μ + , V \mu^{+,V} (the μ i ⋅ \mu^{\cdot}_{i} of Eq. ( 7 ), index i i dropped) and token deviation δ i , t + , V \delta^{+,V}_{i,t} , and analogously for the other views, then c i , t c_{i,t} depends only on the differences ( μ + , V − μ − , V ) (\mu^{+,V}-\mu^{-,V}) and ( μ + , ∅ − μ − , ∅ ) (\mu^{+,\varnothing}-\mu^{-,\varnothing}) , not on the absolute levels μ + , V \mu^{+,V} or μ − , V \mu^{-,V} themselves. The construction thus removes shared offsets and retains the correctness-aligned contrast; whether this reduces sensitivity to policy drift in practice depends on how much of the drift is shared across paired views, which we examine below at the batch level. The token contrast can still be positive or negative on average across a trajectory, depending on whether the response as a whole supports the correct answer more than the incorrect one. Empirical verification. Figure 5 a tracks these quantities during training. The vision gap, a single-view signal, rises from 0.20 to 0.42 (first vs. last 20 steps), while the batch means of Δ \Delta and Δ ¯ \bar{\Delta} stay within 0.02 of zero and shift by at most 0.011; in a separate RLSD run (not plotted), the teacher–student gap drifts from − 0.019 -0.019 to − 0.055 -0.055 . At the batch level, most of the drift is therefore shared by the paired hint views, as the cancellation argument requires. These are batch means, so they do not rule out token- or view-specific shifts; measuring the variance of c i , t c_{i,t} across steps relative to that of the individual view log-probabilities remains future work. B.5 Adaptive Trajectory Confidence: Implementation Details This appendix specifies how the normalized confidence z i z_{i} in Eq. ( 8 ) is implemented and the rationale for making the normalization batch-relative and robust. Estimator. Within each actor micro-batch ℬ \mathcal{B} , let 𝒱 ⊆ ℬ \mathcal{V}\subseteq\mathcal{B} be the rows with a valid hint pair. In the actual implementation, the denominator of Eq. ( 8 ) is rescaled by the constant 1.4826 1.4826 and stabilized by a small constant ϵ \epsilon : z i = clip ⁡ ( S i − med 𝒱 ⁡ ( S ) 1.4826 ​ MAD 𝒱 ​ ( S ) + ϵ , − ζ , ζ ) . z_{i}=\operatorname{clip}\!\Big(\frac{S_{i}-\operatorname{med}_{\mathcal{V}}(S)}{1.4826\,\operatorname{MAD}_{\mathcal{V}}(S)+\epsilon},\,-\zeta,\,\zeta\Big). The factor 1.4826 ≈ 1 / Φ − 1 ​ ( 3 / 4 ) 1.4826\approx 1/\Phi^{-1}(3/4) , where Φ − 1 \Phi^{-1} is the standard normal quantile function, makes 1.4826 ​ MAD 1.4826\,\operatorname{MAD} a consistent estimator of the standard deviation when S S is normally distributed, so z i z_{i} lives on the same scale as an ordinary z z -score and the clip bound ζ = 3 \zeta{=}3 retains its usual “three-sigma” meaning. The constant ϵ \epsilon only prevents division by zero when nearly all values of S S in 𝒱 \mathcal{V} coincide and the MAD vanishes. Three boundary cases are handled explicitly: 1. If a batch has no reward variance ( std ⁡ ( { r j } j ∈ ℬ ) = 0 \operatorname{std}(\{r_{j}\}_{j\in\mathcal{B}})=0 ), all responses are equivalent; we set A i = 0 A_{i}=0 for all i i and skip the RLVR update. 2. If a response has no valid negative sibling ( K i = 0 K_{i}=0 , so the sum in Eq. ( 4 ) is undefined), we use single-view RLSD weights (Eq. ( 2 )) at mixing rate λ i = λ min \lambda_{i}=\lambda_{\min} , a weaker fallback than the pairwise method. 3. If | 𝒱 | < 4 |\mathcal{V}|<4 (too few valid hint pairs for a stable normalization), every valid row receives the neutral value η i = 0.5 \eta_{i}=0.5 ; rows without any hint use uniform GRPO credit. Why batch-relative: tracking the current level. The absolute level of the confidence S i S_{i} changes over training, because the policy — and hence the distribution of sampled responses that the teacher scores — keeps moving. An absolute criterion is therefore fragile: in preliminary experiments, a fixed threshold on S S collapsed, with the mixing rate saturating once the overall level shifted. The batch median acts as the current water level : the normalization only answers whether a trajectory is strong or weak relative to its current batch , so a shift common to the whole batch does not change z i z_{i} . Why median/MAD: heavy tails. The distribution of S i S_{i} is heavy-tailed — on a few trajectories the teacher is extremely confident and produces outlier values of S i S_{i} . Standardizing with mean/std lets those outliers inflate the scale and compresses the z z -scores of the vast majority of ordinary trajectories into a narrow band, destroying the resolution of the normalized confidence exactly where it matters. The median and MAD are robust to such outliers, so the bulk of the distribution keeps full discriminative resolution. Why clipping and the sigmoid midpoint. Clipping z i z_{i} to [ − 3 , 3 ] [-3,3] keeps the sigmoid away from its saturating regimes, so λ i \lambda_{i} is never pinned to the interval endpoints; throughout training we monitor the quantiles of η i \eta_{i} , and the observed P10/P90 of 0.29 / 0.83 0.29/0.83 confirm that the sigmoid mapping operates in its responsive regime. The midpoint carries an explicit semantics: a trajectory at the batch median ( z i = 0 z_{i}=0 ) receives η i = 0.5 \eta_{i}=0.5 , i.e. λ i = 0.4 \lambda_{i}=0.4 , the midpoint of [ 0.15 , 0.65 ] [0.15,0.65] — a typical trajectory receives a typical mixing rate. Why micro-batch rather than global statistics. The four teacher forward passes for a micro-batch are already in hand when the normalization is computed, so the standardization adds zero communication and negligible compute — measured at 0.1 0.1 – 0.2 0.2 s per training step, about 0.05 % 0.05\% of the step time. A global running estimate would add synchronization across data-parallel ranks and, worse, would compare a trajectory against a stale level that lags the shifting distribution, partially reintroducing the sensitivity to drift that batch-relative standardization avoids. Limitations: confidence vs. visual necessity. S i S_{i} reflects the teacher’s full-information confidence rather than whether the response actually needs the image. A response on which the teacher is confident due to the correct hint alone will still receive a fairly high S i S_{i} : removing the image lowers μ i + , ∅ \mu^{+,\varnothing}_{i} only slightly, so only the μ i − , V \mu^{-,V}_{i} and μ i − , ∅ \mu^{-,\varnothing}_{i} terms separate the full-information view from the rest. Two points qualify what adaptive trajectory confidence provides: 1. If the image is irrelevant to a response, then Δ i , t ≈ Δ ¯ i , t \Delta_{i,t}\approx\bar{\Delta}_{i,t} and the token contrast reduces to c i , t ≈ ( α + β ) ​ Δ i , t c_{i,t}\approx(\alpha+\beta)\Delta_{i,t} , a pure answer-correctness contrast. A high mixing rate on such a trajectory still redistributes credit by correctness, but not by visual grounding. 2. Adaptive trajectory confidence therefore acts as a plausibility check on the teacher’s overall quality rather than a guarantee of visual grounding: it down-weights the token contrast mainly on trajectories where the teacher barely separates the full-information view from the degraded ones. These properties hold at the coefficient level , i.e., in the explicit formulas before policy optimization. However, the GRPO objective (Eq. ( 13 )) contains min ⁡ ( ρ i , t ​ A ^ i , t , ρ ¯ i , t ​ A ^ i , t ) \min(\rho_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i,t},\bar{\rho}_{i,t}\hat{A}_{i,t}) and implicit policy gradient clipping. These are non-linear operations. Therefore, after policy optimization: • The actual gradient flow to individual tokens depends on which term in the min ⁡ ( ⋅ ) \min(\cdot) is active (a function of importance weights ρ i , t \rho_{i,t} and ρ ¯ i , t \bar{\rho}_{i,t} ). • The magnitude of token-level updates is not directly controlled by the coefficient structure; it depends on the clipping regime and the distribution of advantage magnitudes. • The properties guarantee that the direction and sign of credit assignment remain aligned with the trajectory-level verifier reward, and that credit is redistributed (not amplified) among tokens. But they do not guarantee that the final update magnitudes will preserve the exact mean or relative weighting structure after clipping. In summary, the sign- and mean-preserving properties hold at the coefficient level and ensure that the verifier reward controls the overall optimization direction. The token contrast cannot flip the sign or amplify the trajectory advantage. However, the effect size of individual token updates within a trajectory is not fully determined by the coefficient structure and depends on the policy gradient dynamics. B.7 Training Dynamics Figure 4: Training dynamics of PACE, RLSD, and GRPO on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct over the shared 200-step budget. Top: overall training reward, i.e. the fraction of sampled responses passing the verifier. Bottom: mean response length in tokens. Light traces show raw values and bold curves show smoothed trends. Figure 4 tracks the overall training reward and the mean response length of PACE, RLSD, and GRPO over the 200-step budget. The reward curves are close throughout: they rise from about 0.20 to 0.39, PACE is slightly ahead between roughly steps 120 and 170 (peaking near 0.41), and the three converge again by step 200. The training reward therefore does not separate the methods; the differences in Table 1 appear only on held-out benchmarks. Response length orders the methods more clearly. All three compress responses sharply during the first 50 steps, from about 2,000 tokens to 500–900. GRPO compresses fastest, stays near 500 tokens until step 150, and then re-inflates to about 800 tokens by step 200. RLSD compresses slowest and stays above PACE from about step 110 on. PACE compresses at an intermediate rate, remains flat at 600–700 tokens, and ends with the shortest responses (about 620 tokens at step 200). The curves describe rather than explain the effect of token credit; the component-level evidence comes from the ablations (Table 2 ). Inset: zoomed view of the hint contrasts. (b) Mixing rate λ i \lambda_{i} (median and P10–P90 band) and raw confidence S i S_{i} . Vision gap drifts but pairwise token contrast does not. Figure 5 a tracks the vision gap and hint contrasts during training. The vision gap doubles from 0.20 to 0.42 as the teacher improves: its full-vision log-probabilities pull away from null-vision ones, and this shift enters the signal directly regardless of whether a token depends on the image. The hint contrasts stay within 0.02 of zero and move by at most 0.011, about 20 × \times less than the vision gap. The drift is shared by both hint branches of each contrast and cancels in subtraction. A 0.4 drift produces weight factors e 0.4 ≈ 1.49 e^{0.4}\approx 1.49 that exceed the clip bound u max u_{\max} , flattening token differences and explaining why the vision-gap variant falls below Base. Adaptive trajectory confidence is batch-relative. Figure 5 b shows that while the raw confidence S i S_{i} rises from 0.23 to 0.34 as the teacher grows more confident, the distribution of the mixing rate λ i \lambda_{i} remains stable: the P10–P90 band stays at 0.30–0.57 and the median at 0.40 throughout training. The robust batch-relative standardization absorbs both the level and scale drift of S i S_{i} , so adaptive trajectory confidence ranks trajectories by confidence relative to the current batch rather than shifting credit toward the token contrast as training progresses. B.9 Training-Time Cost Analysis Figure 6: Per-step training and generation time across RLVR methods on an 8 × \times NVIDIA H200 GPU cluster. (a) Total step time. (b) Generation time. Figure 6 reports the empirical per-step training and generation time across RLVR methods on an 8 × \times NVIDIA H200 GPU cluster. The pairwise token contrast of PACE requires positive and negative teacher contexts under both full and nulled vision. With one negative hint, this corresponds to four scored contexts per response, implemented as sequential microbatches to bound memory use. After the first 50 steps, a PACE step takes about 350–380 s, compared with about 250–280 s for GRPO and 300–350 s for RLSD and RLCSD, and far less than PAPO (about 800 s) and VPPO (about 1,000 s). Generation time (panel b) is close to that of GRPO (about 50 s per step), so the overhead comes from teacher scoring rather than from longer rollouts. The additional computational work is confined strictly to training; evaluation and deployment use the original policy alone without any overhead. Appendix D Case Study Figures 7 – 9 visualize token credit on three responses from the evaluation benchmarks. For each response, the upper copy shows the token weights assigned by PACE and the lower copy those assigned by RLSD on the same sampled tokens; darker shading marks a larger weight, i.e. a larger share of the trajectory advantage. Both methods keep the sign and mean of the trajectory advantage, so the figures differ only in where credit is placed within the response. Credit on visual readouts (Figure 7 ). The MathVista question asks how many items sold more than 3 units in at least one store of a grouped bar chart. The response reads both bars for all seven items and concludes that all seven qualify. PACE shades the values read from the chart (e.g., 9 for violin , 7 for arch , 1 for breeze ), the comparison token “both”, and the final count “All 7”. RLSD instead highlights tokens that restate the question (“either”, “exceeding”, “sold”) and leaves the chart readouts nearly unweighted. The contrast between correct and incorrect hints singles out the tokens that decide the count, rather than restating the question. Credit on computation (Figure 8 ). The LogicVista question asks for Website Y’s share of visitors in a table. The response copies the four visitor counts, sums them to 437,380, and divides to obtain 18.86%, which it rounds to option (B). PACE places its largest weights on the result-bearing tokens: the copied counts (e.g., 315,380), the distinguishing digit of the total, the quotient digits of 0.1886, and the decision tokens “Percentage =”, “Therefore”, “correct answer”, and “(B”. RLSD concentrates on the connective phrase “me compute this” and on “=” and “Therefore”, and assigns nearly uniform weight to the copied counts. Credit on an incorrect response (Figure 9 ). The third response is incorrect: it reads 58.09% and 44.00% for the bottom two countries and answers 51.05 instead of 51.04. Its arithmetic is consistent with these readouts, so the error lies in the extracted values or the rounding. Because the trajectory advantage is negative, a larger weight here means a larger share of the penalty. PACE concentrates the penalty on the extracted values and their context (“Madagascar:”, the digits of 58.09 and 44.00, “from 2012”) and on “percentages”, while RLSD spreads it over planning tokens such as “first”, “which”, “bar”, “These”, and “Next”. Concentrating the penalty on the readouts, rather than on generic planning steps, spares the parts of the reasoning that are correct. blocks.en: Figure 4 tracks the overall training reward and the mean response length of PACE, RLSD, and GRPO over the 200-step budget. The reward curves are close throughout: they rise from about 0.20 to 0.39, PACE is slightly ahead between roughly steps 120 and 170 (peaking near 0.41), and the three converge again by step 200. The training reward therefore does not separate the methods; the differences in Table 1 appear only on held-out benchmarks.
blocks.zh: 图4记录了PACE、RLSD和GRPO在200步预算中的总体培训奖励和平均响应时间。 奖励曲线全程相近:它们从约0.20起升至0.39起,PACE在大约120至170步之间略为领先(峰值接近0.41起),而三步又以200步再次会合. 因此,培训奖励没有将方法分开;表1中的差异只出现在搁置的基准上。

blocks.en: Response length orders the methods more clearly. All three compress responses sharply during the first 50 steps, from about 2,000 tokens to 500–900. GRPO compresses fastest, stays near 500 tokens until step 150, and then re-inflates to about 800 tokens by step 200. RLSD compresses slowest and stays above PACE from about step 110 on. PACE compresses at an intermediate rate, remains flat at 600–700 tokens, and ends with the shortest responses (about 620 tokens at step 200). The curves describe rather than explain the effect of token credit; the component-level evidence comes from the ablations (Table 2 ).

blocks.en: Figure 6 reports the empirical per-step training and generation time across RLVR methods on an 8 × \times NVIDIA H200 GPU cluster. The pairwise token contrast of PACE requires positive and negative teacher contexts under both full and nulled vision. With one negative hint, this corresponds to four scored contexts per response, implemented as sequential microbatches to bound memory use. After the first 50 steps, a PACE step takes about 350–380 s, compared with about 250–280 s for GRPO and 300–350 s for RLSD and RLCSD, and far less than PAPO (about 800 s) and VPPO (about 1,000 s). Generation time (panel b) is close to that of GRPO (about 50 s per step), so the overhead comes from teacher scoring rather than from longer rollouts. The additional computational work is confined strictly to training; evaluation and deployment use the original policy alone without any overhead.

blocks.en: C.2 Results on Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct
blocks.zh: C.2 Quen3-VL-2B-指示的结果

blocks.en: On Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (Table 5 ), PACE is second on average (38.23%, +4.19 over Base) behind RLSD (38.78%). It is best on GSM8K-V and LogicVista but trails RLSD on MMMU, MathVision, and MathVista, and falls below Base on MathVista (55.60 vs. 58.36), as GRPO does (52.33). We attribute this to the 2B model’s limited capacity as a self-teacher. The training data—filtered to retain only problems that the much larger Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking consistently fails—is too difficult for 2B to reliably solve even with privileged hints. When the 2B teacher itself produces low-confidence or inconsistent predictions under correct-answer contexts, the pairwise contrasts degrade into uninformative noise, and the confidence S i S_{i} used by adaptive trajectory confidence becomes unreliable. Token-level credit assignment thus provides less benefit over uniform GRPO when the teacher capacity is insufficient relative to task difficulty.
blocks.zh: 在Qwen3-VL-2B-指令(表5)上,PACE平均排在RLSD(38.78%)后第二位(38.23%,+4.19比Base). 它最好在GSM8K-V和LogicVista上,但在MMMU, MathVision,和 MathVista上追踪到RLSD, 并像GRPO(52.33)一样在MathVista上低于Base(55.60 vs 58.36). 我们将此归因于2B模式作为自我教师的能力有限。 所过滤的训练数据仅保留了更大的Qune3-VL-4B-思维一贯失败的问题,即使有特殊暗示,2B也难以可靠地解决。 当2B老师自己在正确答案上下文下产生低信心或不一致的预测时,双相对比会降解为非成形噪声,而适应性轨迹自信所使用的信心S i S_{i}变得不可靠. 因此,当教师能力相对于工作难度而言不足时,分配的托肯级信贷比统一的GRPO提供的福利较少。

blocks.en: The MathVista question asks how many items sold more than 3 units in at least one store of a grouped bar chart. The response reads both bars for all seven items and concludes that all seven qualify. PACE shades the values read from the chart (e.g., 9 for violin , 7 for arch , 1 for breeze ), the comparison token “both”, and the final count “All 7”. RLSD instead highlights tokens that restate the question (“either”, “exceeding”, “sold”) and leaves the chart readouts nearly unweighted. The contrast between correct and incorrect hints singles out the tokens that decide the count, rather than restating the question.
blocks.zh: MathVista质疑至少有一商店的组合条形图中售出超过3个单元的物品数量. 答复中为所有7个项目读出两个条并得出结论,所有7个项目都符合条件。 计算机设备行动伙伴关系对图表中的数值进行遮蔽(例如:小提琴为9个;拱门为7个;微风为1个);比较符号“两者”和最后计数“所有7个”。 反之,RLSD突出强调了重复问题(“或者”、“超越”、“出售”)的标志,使图表的读取几乎没有加权。 正确与不正确的提示之间的对比,会挑出决定计数的符号,而不是重述问题.

blocks.en: The LogicVista question asks for Website Y’s share of visitors in a table. The response copies the four visitor counts, sums them to 437,380, and divides to obtain 18.86%, which it rounds to option (B). PACE places its largest weights on the result-bearing tokens: the copied counts (e.g., 315,380), the distinguishing digit of the total, the quotient digits of 0.1886, and the decision tokens “Percentage =”, “Therefore”, “correct answer”, and “(B”. RLSD concentrates on the connective phrase “me compute this” and on “=” and “Therefore”, and assigns nearly uniform weight to the copied counts.
blocks.zh: LogicVista 问及网站Y的访客份额。 答复复制了这4名访客的数量,共计437 380人,除以18.86%,然后进行选择(B)。 计算机设备行动伙伴关系将最大权重放在有结果的符号上:复制的计数(例如,315 380)、总数字的区别、0.1886的商数和决定符号“百分比=”、“因此”、“正确答案”和“B”。 RLSD专注于连接词“me compute this”和“=”和“因此”,并给所复制的计数分配几乎一致的权重。

blocks.en: The third response is incorrect: it reads 58.09% and 44.00% for the bottom two countries and answers 51.05 instead of 51.04. Its arithmetic is consistent with these readouts, so the error lies in the extracted values or the rounding. Because the trajectory advantage is negative, a larger weight here means a larger share of the penalty. PACE concentrates the penalty on the extracted values and their context (“Madagascar:”, the digits of 58.09 and 44.00, “from 2012”) and on “percentages”, while RLSD spreads it over planning tokens such as “first”, “which”, “bar”, “These”, and “Next”. Concentrating the penalty on the readouts, rather than on generic planning steps, spares the parts of the reasoning that are correct.
blocks.zh: 第三个答复是不正确的:最底层两个国家的答复分别为58.09%和44.00%,回答51.05而不是51.04. 它的算术与这些读取一致,所以出错在于取出值或取出四舍五入. 由于轨迹优势为负值,因此这里较大的重量意味着更大比例的罚分. PACE将惩罚集中在提取值及其上下文(“马达加斯加:,58.09和44.00的位数,“从2012年起”)和“百分比”,而RSD则将其分布在诸如“第一”、“第一”、“第二”、“第二”、“第二”等规划标志上。 将惩罚集中在宣读上,而不是放在一般的规划步骤上,就省去了推理中正确之处。

blocks.en: These examples are qualitative and were selected for illustration, which show how the two signals differ in placement, not that PACE assigns credit correctly on every response.
blocks.zh: 这些实例是定性的,被选作示例,说明两种信号在放置上有何不同,而不是PACE在每个响应上正确分配信用.
